description: In-app public surface: remove the two obsolete PUBLIC destinations that send customers into the staff workspace, add a reject-by-default local return-path validator as a new standalone module, and pin all of it plus the existing 404 home-fallback contract with vitest guards. Independent of FEAT-002 (that one is the hosting layer and live AWS), but ordered first so the tree is green before any production write. Touches NO file owned by another workstream: src/pages/account/**, src/lib/customerAuth.ts, src/lib/dialCodes.ts, src/components/HeaderCart.tsx, src/components/PhoneField.tsx and amplify/** are all left alone.
steps: READ FIRST: .agents/tasks/url-host-cleanup/context.json and .agents/tasks/url-host-cleanup/plan.md sections 0.8, 0.9, 1 (D6) and 2 steps 1-6. Do not re-derive what context.json already states.

Create src/lib/safeReturnPath.ts exporting `safeLocalReturnPath( raw: string | null | undefined ): string`. Reject-by-default allowlist: return a member of { '/cart/', '/checkout/', '/orders/', '/shop/', '/account/', '/' } (match with and without the trailing slash, normalise to the slashed form) or the default '/cart/'. Reject BEFORE any match, in this order: not starting with exactly one '/'; a second leading '/' or '\\' (blocks //evil, //evil.example, ///evil, /\evil); any backslash, whitespace, control character, '%', '?', '#' or ':' anywhere; any '..' path segment; and any path whose FIRST segment is one of workspace, admin, access, dashboard, dm, engage, settings, task, seo, commerce, pay, forms, service, contacts, docs. Do NOT URL-decode the input - decoding is what turns %2f%2f into a bypass, so reject '%' outright and compare the raw string. Mirror the shape of safeHttpHref in src/lib/randomToken.ts: RETURN THE VALUE TO USE, never a boolean, so a caller cannot validate one string and navigate to another. Document in the file header why each rejection class exists and that the module has no production caller yet (the wiring belongs to the src/pages/account/** owner).

Create src/test/SafeReturnPath.test.ts. Rejected cases that must each return '/cart/': 'https://evil.example/', '//evil.example', '//evil', '///evil', '/\\evil.example', '\\\\evil.example', '%2f%2fevil.example', '%252f%252fevil', '/cart/%0d%0aSet-Cookie:x', '/cart/\t', '/ cart/', '/../etc/passwd', '/cart/../workspace/access', 'javascript:alert(1)', 'data:text/html,x', 'mailto:a@b', '/workspace/access', '/workspace/dashboard/', '/admin/', '/dashboard/', '/settings/', '', null, undefined. Accepted cases: '/cart/', '/cart', '/checkout/', '/orders/', '/shop/', '/account/', '/'. Add one case asserting an accepted return value never carries a query string or fragment.

Edit src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx: change handleGoHome (line ~38) from `window.location.href = '/workspace/dashboard'` to `window.location.href = '/'`, and relabel the secondary button (line ~72) from 'Dashboard' to 'Home'. Leave handleReload, the component props and the styles untouched. Add a short dated comment recording that this component is mounted inside the `if ( isPublic )` branch of src/pages/_app.tsx, so the old target offered a customer a button into the staff login. Before editing, grep src/test for 'handleGoHome' and for the 'Dashboard' button label to confirm no existing test pins the old value.

Edit public/manifest.json: delete the three `shortcuts` entries whose url is /workspace/dashboard/, /workspace/engage/inbox/ or /workspace/contacts/. If that leaves shortcuts empty, remove the key entirely rather than leaving []. Change nothing else - name, short_name, icons, start_url, display, theme_color, background_color all stay exactly as they are.

Create src/test/PublicWorkspaceLinks.test.ts following the read-source-as-text technique of src/test/PublicRouteRegistration.test.ts (importing _app.tsx would execute Amplify.configure). Assert: (a) src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx contains no '/workspace' substring; (b) public/manifest.json, parsed, has no string value starting '/workspace'; (c) src/components/Header.tsx and src/components/Footer.tsx contain no href to /workspace, /admin, /access or sign-in. Include an INTENTIONALLY_WORKSPACE_ONLY map naming src/components/Layout.tsx, src/components/SearchModal.tsx, src/components/ui/Breadcrumbs.tsx and public/sw.js with a one-line reason each is exempt (the first three are imported only by src/pages/workspace/**; sw.js:180 is a staff push-notification destination, not a navigation link, and is recorded as needs-verification rather than changed).

Create src/test/NotFoundFallback.test.ts asserting from the source text of src/pages/404.tsx that it calls router.replace with a LITERAL '/' (not a template literal and not a variable, so no path, query or fragment can ever be forwarded), that it declares <meta name="robots" content="noindex, follow">, and that its canonical is https://wecare.digital/. src/pages/404.tsx itself needs NO code change - it was read and verified against live HTTP; this test pins that behaviour so a later edit cannot quietly start forwarding untrusted input.
Run the gates: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npx vitest run. Fix anything that breaks.

Set this feature's status to 'completed' in this file and record in `findings`: the exact files changed, whether any pre-existing test had to be updated, and the ready-to-apply one-line wiring for src/pages/account/sign-in.tsx so FEAT-002 can copy it verbatim into the matrix document.
acceptance_criteria: src/lib/safeReturnPath.ts exists and exports safeLocalReturnPath returning a path string, never a boolean.
npx vitest run src/test/SafeReturnPath.test.ts passes, and the suite includes an explicit '//evil' case and an explicit '/workspace/access' case, both returning '/cart/'.
src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx contains no '/workspace' string and its secondary button reads 'Home'.
public/manifest.json parses as JSON and contains no value beginning '/workspace'.
npx vitest run src/test/PublicWorkspaceLinks.test.ts and src/test/NotFoundFallback.test.ts both pass.
npm run typecheck exits 0, npm run lint exits 0, npx vitest run exits 0 with no pre-existing test newly failing.

No file under src/pages/account/**, amplify/**, src/lib/customerAuth.ts, src/lib/dialCodes.ts, src/components/HeaderCart.tsx or src/components/PhoneField.tsx was modified (confirm with git status --short).
verification: npx vitest run src/test/SafeReturnPath.test.ts src/test/PublicWorkspaceLinks.test.ts src/test/NotFoundFallback.test.ts
git status --short  (confirm only owned paths changed, and that another session's modified files are untouched)

Its test 'points manifest shortcuts at the canonical workspace URLs rather than a redirect' asserted the exact three-URL array and would have failed. Per repo convention the original rationale was NOT deleted - it is preserved in the comment under a dated SUPERSEDED note, because it is still the correct guidance for the shape workspace shortcuts would take if they ever belong in a manifest again.

=== READY-TO-APPLY WIRING FOR src/pages/account/sign-in.tsx (copy verbatim into the matrix document) ===
In `returnPathFromUrl()` (currently at src/pages/account/sign-in.tsx:170-175), replace line 174
    return /^\/[a-zA-Z0-9/_-]*\/?$/.test( raw ) ? raw : '/cart/';
with
    return safeLocalReturnPath( raw );
and add the import alongside the other src/lib imports:
    import { safeLocalReturnPath } from '../../lib/safeReturnPath';
The line above it (`const raw = String( new URLSearchParams( window.location.search ).get( 'return' ) || '' ).trim();`) and the `typeof window === 'undefined'` early return both stay as they are - safeLocalReturnPath accepts null/undefined/'' and returns '/cart/', so the .trim() and the `|| ''` are now belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing. Also replace the stale comment on line 173 ("Only same-site absolute paths, so this can never be turned into an open redirect") - it is the claim that was FALSE: '//evil' and '/workspace/access' both passed that regex. Two behaviour changes the account/** owner must accept before applying: (1) a local path outside the allowlist (e.g. '/blog/') now goes to '/cart/' instead of being honoured, and (2) an unslashed accepted path is normalised ('/cart' -> '/cart/') rather than returned as typed.
